snippet.title: The Most AI-Pilled CEO We Know
snippet.description:
Brex co-founder and CEO Pedro Franceschi believes most people still underestimate how much AI will change the way companies are built. AI isn't just another tool, it's a new foundation for building products, teams, and companies.

In this episode of Lightcone, Pedro shares why he thinks we're only months into a platform shift as significant as the invention of electricity, how AI has changed the way he works, and why every founder should be "token maxing" to understand the limits of the technology firsthand.

He explains why the CEO needs to be the chief AI officer, how Brex is rebuilding itself around AI, and why founders should rethink what's possible when intelligence is available on demand.

Apply to Y Combinator: https://www.ycombinator.com/apply
Work at a startup: https://www.ycombinator.com/jobs

snippet.title: How Legora Went From YC to $100M ARR in 18 Months
snippet.description:
Max Junestrand was a college student in Sweden with a McKinsey offer in his back pocket. Instead, he and two co-founders went all in on legal AI — and built Legora (YC W24) into one of the fastest-growing enterprise companies in history, surpassing $100M in ARR in just 18 months. Today, Legora is one of Europe's most valuable AI startups, recently valued at $5.6B, with close to 500 employees serving 1,000+ organizations across 50+ markets.

In this fireside with YC General Partner Gustaf Alströmer at our Stockholm event in April, Max shares how Legora found its way into legal AI, why it moved so fast after YC, and how it convinced one of the world's most conservative industries to embrace a new way of working. He also digs into fundraising, competing in the age of foundation models, scaling a founder-led culture, and why Legora's ambition goes far beyond legal tech.

Apply to Y Combinator: https://www.ycombinator.com/apply
Work at a Startup: https://www.ycombinator.com/jobs

snippet.title: Adding voice control to my cyberdeck!
snippet.description:
This is my first time building a voice interface and hardware

A few weeks ago I didn’t know what an ESP32 was, where assets lived in firmware, or what “flashing a device” meant

I started with an existing codebase and asked Codex a lot of beginner questions

I replaced the assets with makeup tutorials, reorganized the interface, added voice commands, and somehow ended up with a tiny makeup cyberdeck that responds to “mirror mirror” 🥺

Hardware is humbling but it’s been a lot of fun ⊹₊｡ꕤ˚

snippet.title: What Actually Makes You an AI Engineer
snippet.description:
Why do so many aspiring AI engineers stay stuck? They focus on the tool, not the concept. The AI tooling ecosystem moves incredibly fast — new libraries, frameworks, and model providers drop every single week. If your knowledge is tied to one tool's API, you're on a treadmill, constantly relearning the next thing. 

Focus on the underlying concepts instead. When you understand the concepts, you can pick up any tool extremely quickly, but when you only learn the tool, you start from scratch every time. 

Frameworks are just implementations of the details — the concepts are what make you an actual engineer.

#techwithtim #learntocode #aiengineer #programming

snippet.title: How designers steal (without getting caught)
snippet.description:
you can’t prompt good design if you don’t recognize good design 🤭

steal like a designer (the right way) with mobbin design

for me this usually starts outside of software

i study mechanics in the real world like how things move, how they reveal info, how they respond to touch. sometimes i’ll take those ideas and try translating them into a digital experience

- a music box crank
- tearing off a calendar page
- opening an envelope

the second thing i do is pattern training and see how different apps solve the same problems 

this is where mobbin has been really helpful for me because you can quickly browse real screens and flows from a ton of products in one place

and honestly that mostly comes down to repetition! doing it again and again until your brain starts building its own mental library

anyway these are just some small things that helped me train my design eye over time 🪩

the second thing i do is pattern training and see how different apps solve the same problems 

this is where mobbin has been really helpful for me because you can quickly browse real screens and flows from a ton of products in one place

and honestly that mostly comes down to repetition! doing it again and again until your brain starts building its own mental library

anyway these are just some small things that helped me train my design eye over time 🪩

snippet.title: 3 OpenClaw Setup That Will 10x Your Output
snippet.description:
Three OpenClaw setups that will change how much you can get done, and I'll drop the exact prompts so you can set these up yourself.

Quick reminder before anything, only do this if you understand how permissions and security work. OpenClaw is powerful, and you want to know what you're handing it access to. 

First — Custom Mission Control. This is your home base. Instead of OpenClaw being a general-purpose agent, you set it up with a specific mission - your goals, your priorities, your workflows, your preferences. Think of it like onboarding a new team member, except you write the onboarding doc yourself. The more specific you are about how you work and what matters, the more useful every single interaction becomes. This one setup changes everything downstream.

Second — Discord Setup. You connect OpenClaw to your Discord, and it becomes an active participant in your server, monitoring channels, flagging things that need your attention, and executing tasks based on what's happening in real time. If your team lives in Discord, this turns OpenClaw from a tool you go to into something that's already in the room with you.

Third — Multi-Agent Framework. Instead of one agent doing everything, you set up multiple specialized agents that each handle a specific type of task - one for research, one for file management, one for communications and they work in parallel. The output you can get from a well-structured multi-agent setup is genuinely hard to believe until you see it running.

All three of these prompts are linked in the video description, grab them and try it yourself.

Which setup are you starting with? Drop it in the comments 👇

snippet.title: Learn CSS in 5 Minutes (Seriously)
snippet.description:
Learn CSS in this CSS tutorial for beginners! This CSS crash course is the best way to learn CSS fast. If you want to learn to code and get into web development, this is for you. This is a simple CSS tutorial and a complete CSS overview. Learn front end development and become a software developer with this introduction to CSS. This video will teach you how to learn CSS with no experience.

Unlock the power of web design and learn CSS in just 5 minutes! This video is your fast track to understanding the fundamentals of Cascading Style Sheets (CSS), the language that brings websites to life. If you're looking to get started with web development, front end development, or simply want to learn to code, this is the perfect starting point.

This CSS tutorial for beginners is designed to be a CSS crash course that will teach you the essentials of CSS without any fluff. We'll dive straight into the core concepts you need to know, making this the best way to learn CSS fast. Whether you have no experience or are looking for a quick refresher, this easy CSS tutorial for beginners will get you up and running with CSS coding in no time.

Forget long, complicated tutorials. This video provides a CSS overview that is both concise and comprehensive. You'll gain a solid understanding of how CSS works with HTML to create beautiful and responsive websites. We'll cover key topics that are essential for any aspiring web developer.

What you'll learn in this video:
• Introduction to CSS: A quick rundown of what CSS is and why it's crucial for web development.
• Getting Started With CSS: Learn how to add CSS to your HTML files.
• CSS Box Model Explained: Understand the fundamental concept of the CSS box model.
• CSS Display Property Explained: A simple explanation of the display property and how to use it.
• CSS Tricks and basic styling.
• This video is your first step to mastering front-end development. If you're serious about becoming a software developer, understanding CSS is non-negotiable.
